Examination ERP MVP Architecture

Technical design and data model  
Entropix Systems | Product and engineering team

# 1 Architecture decision

The MVP uses a modular monolith with a React web client, NestJS REST API, PostgreSQL and private object storage. One codebase contains domain modules and a separately runnable background worker. The database is the source of truth for state transitions, result snapshots and queued work.

This is a proposed technical architecture for the owned Examination ERP SaaS. The interactive mock UI is a separate static demonstration; it does not implement this backend.

## Components and responsibilities

| **Component** | **Choice**                           | **Responsibility**                                                                  |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Web           | React, TypeScript, Vite, MUI         | Role-aware pages, forms, tables, responsive attendance and student views.           |
| Client data   | TanStack Query, React Hook Form, Zod | Server cache, form state, immediate validation; server repeats all validations.     |
| API           | NestJS, TypeScript, REST, OpenAPI    | Authentication, authorization, domain commands, queries and transaction boundaries. |
| Data access   | Prisma and reviewed SQL migrations   | Typed queries, transaction wrapper, composite constraints and RLS policies.         |
| Database      | PostgreSQL                           | Tenant data, rule versions, workflow state, audit and durable job/outbox records.   |
| Files         | Private S3 compatible storage        | Quarantined uploads, clean documents and immutable generated PDF versions.          |
| Worker        | Same repository and domain libraries | PDF rendering, imports, result computation and email retries.                       |
| Delivery      | Docker, GitHub Actions, AWS pilot    | Reproducible builds, controlled migrations, health checks and rollback.             |

## Deployment topology

Browser traffic reaches a TLS gateway. It serves static frontend assets and routes /api/v1 to the API container. The API and worker share a private database and object store; an email adapter is the only required outbound business integration. Do not put database credentials, private bucket URLs or service secrets in the frontend.

Use one API instance and one worker for a small controlled pilot, with a managed private database and backups. This is not an HA design or an exam-day availability guarantee. Scale and availability changes require measured load and recovery results.

# 2 Domain boundaries and data flow

## Modules

Identity owns principals, sessions and tenant memberships. Academics owns structure, profiles and subject enrolments. Exams owns exam rules and registrations. Scheduling owns papers, hall sittings, seats and invigilator duties. Conduct owns attendance and incidents. Evaluation owns assignments, component marks and approval batches. Results owns versioned computations and publication. Documents, Notifications and Audit provide shared services.

Controllers call domain services. A module exposes commands and queries; another module must not update its tables directly. The application layer coordinates commands that require one transaction. Query endpoints may join read models while preserving scope.

## Critical request path

Authenticate session → resolve active tenant membership → enforce action permission and department/assignment scope → validate command and expected version → execute database transaction → record audit and outbox → commit → return updated version. External calls happen after commit in a worker.

## Publication consistency

A result run references the exact exam rule version and an input revision counter. Any registration, attendance, incident hold or marks change that can affect results increments that counter in the same transaction. A worker reads a consistent input snapshot and writes an immutable candidate result run.

Publication locks the exam row, verifies that the candidate input revision still equals the current revision and that all approval gates still pass, then updates the active publication pointer and appends audit/outbox records atomically. Duplicate publish commands return the same publication. A stale run returns 409 RESULT_INPUT_CHANGED.

## Background processing

Use a PostgreSQL job/outbox table rather than adding Redis for the MVP. Workers claim eligible rows with row locks and SKIP LOCKED, set a lease expiry and commit the claim before performing slow work. Expired leases are reclaimable. Results and documents use unique business keys to make processing idempotent.

Delivery is at least once. Email submission can be ambiguous after a timeout; record UNKNOWN and reconcile if provider support exists. Never claim exactly-once external delivery. Retry transient failures after 1, 5 and 15 minutes, then mark failed with a manual retry action. A failed email must not roll back a published result.

# 3 Tenant and identity security

## Tenant isolation

All business tables carry tenant_id. Global tables are limited to authentication principals and platform institution metadata. API handlers obtain tenant context from the authenticated session and a verified membership, never from an unchecked request body or hostname.

Every parent exposes a unique (tenant_id, id) key and every business relationship uses a matching composite foreign key. Unique roll numbers and codes are tenant-scoped. List, search, count, download, export and worker operations require the same scope as mutations.

## Database enforcement

Enable and force PostgreSQL row-level security for tenant tables. The runtime role must not own tables, be superuser or have BYPASSRLS. A separate migration role owns schema changes. Policies use tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::uuid for both USING and WITH CHECK; absent context must deny access.

The application executes tenant queries inside a transaction, sets context with parameterized set_config(..., true), and passes the transaction client into every repository. Transaction-local context prevents pooled connections retaining another tenant's setting. No unscoped Prisma client is available to tenant repositories or workers. RLS complements authorization and does not replace role/assignment checks. \[T1\]

## Authentication proposal

Provision accounts with expiring, single-use invite links. Use established password hashing, rate-limited login/reset endpoints and generic failure messages. Do not email plaintext passwords. Keep short-lived access tokens in memory and a rotating refresh token in a Secure HttpOnly SameSite cookie. Store only refresh-token hashes; revoke the token family on replay, password reset or deactivation. Verify Origin and CSRF protection on cookie-authenticated mutations.

Proposed defaults are 15-minute access tokens, 7-day refresh expiry and 24-hour invites; lock these through configuration and tests. Persist a server-side session record and verify membership is active on each request so suspension does not wait for token expiry.

## Authorization

Permission guards protect each endpoint. Domain services additionally check the requested resource, department, assignment and workflow state. Hidden navigation is convenience only. Return 404 for inaccessible object IDs to reduce existence disclosure; return 403 for a known disallowed action. Platform administration uses separate endpoints without unrestricted impersonation. \[T2\]

# 4 Core data model

Every tenant entity also has id, tenant_id, created_at and updated_at. Mutable aggregates carry version. Business history is retained; deactivation replaces deletion when a record has dependencies. UTC timestamps are displayed in the institution's IANA timezone.

| **Entity**       | **Important fields**                         | **Relationship or invariant**                                                  |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Tenant           | name, slug, status, timezone, plan           | Global platform record; one institution per tenant.                            |
| User and Session | email, password_hash; token_hash, revoked_at | Global principal; no institution access without membership.                    |
| Membership       | user_id, status                              | Unique user and tenant pair.                                                   |
| RoleGrant        | membership_id, role, department_id           | Fixed role with optional department scope.                                     |
| Campus           | code, name                                   | Tenant-scoped unique code.                                                     |
| Department       | campus_id, code                              | Belongs to a campus in the same tenant.                                        |
| Program          | department_id, code                          | College program or school curriculum.                                          |
| AcademicYear     | code, starts_on, ends_on                     | Dates ordered; exam term lies within year.                                     |
| Term             | year_id, program_id, ordinal                 | Semester or annual term; unique program/year/ordinal.                          |
| Cohort           | term_id, code                                | Class or batch section within term.                                            |
| Subject          | program_id, code, title                      | Stable identity; exam stores its assessment configuration.                     |
| Student          | membership_id, roll_no, name, status         | Unique tenant roll number and student membership.                              |
| Faculty          | membership_id, department_id                 | Faculty principal with scoped role grants.                                     |
| Enrolment        | student_id, subject_id, cohort_id, active    | Unique student/subject/cohort; application cannot invent subjects.             |
| Exam             | term_id, mode, state, input_revision         | Aggregate lock for result-affecting changes.                                   |
| ExamSubject      | exam_id, subject_id, credits                 | Unique subject per exam; grading and components bound here.                    |
| RuleVersion      | exam_id, revision, policy_json, hash         | Immutable after registration opens; validated schema, not executable formulas. |

## Academic relationship map

Tenant → Campus → Department → Program → Term → Cohort. AcademicYear also owns Term. Subject belongs to Program; Enrolment joins Student, Subject and Cohort. Exam belongs to Term; ExamSubject joins Exam and Subject. The term reference is the boundary for this MVP's regular attempt.

Student and faculty records store only necessary profile fields. PAN, bank details, biometrics and ICAI membership numbers are absent from this product model.

# 5 Examination and result records

| **Entity**           | **Important fields**                         | **Relationship or invariant**                                                  |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Registration         | exam_id, student_id, state                   | Unique exam/student; mode and eligibility snapshot retained.                   |
| RegistrationSubject  | registration_id, exam_subject_id, state      | Unique pair; approved subjects drive attendance and marks roster.              |
| ExamPaper            | exam_subject_id, start_at, end_at, revision  | One scheduled written sitting per subject in MVP.                              |
| Hall                 | campus_id, code, capacity                    | Positive capacity; immutable allocation snapshot when published.               |
| HallSitting          | paper_id, hall_id, starts_at, ends_at        | Unique paper/hall; overlapping room usage is blocked.                          |
| SeatAssignment       | sitting_id, registration_subject_id, seat_no | Unique sitting/seat and registration-subject; student overlap checked.         |
| Duty                 | sitting_id, faculty_id, status               | Unique assignment; overlapping active duties blocked.                          |
| Attendance           | registration_subject_id, status, marked_by   | One per approved subject; NOT_MARKED is distinct from ABSENT.                  |
| Incident             | paper_id, student_id nullable, state, hold   | Open student-linked cases block that student's result; hall cases need review. |
| EvaluationAssignment | exam_subject_id, faculty_id, due_at          | One active examiner per subject in MVP; reassignment audited.                  |
| MarksBatch           | exam_subject_id, state, submitter, approver  | One active batch; approval by a distinct authorized person.                    |
| Mark                 | registration_subject_id, component, value    | Unique component mark; decimal, nullable when absent or held.                  |
| ResultRun            | exam_id, input_revision, rule_id, status     | Immutable output set with input checksum and validation summary.               |
| ResultItem           | run_id, registration_subject_id, outcome     | Component snapshots, percentage, grade, points and reason.                     |
| StudentResult        | run_id, student_id, outcome, GPA             | Aggregate snapshot, never recomputed at student read time.                     |
| Publication          | exam_id, run_id, status, published_by        | At most one active publication pointer per exam.                               |
| DocumentVersion      | object_key, category, checksum, scan_state   | Immutable version; explicit business binding and audience.                     |
| ImportJob            | kind, file_hash, status, row_counts          | Preview/reject/commit report; duplicate request safe.                          |
| Job and Notification | dedupe_key, lease, attempts; delivery_state  | Durable work and per-recipient notification tracking.                          |
| AuditEvent           | actor, action, target, reason, request_id    | Append-only service permission; redacted change fields.                        |

These are logical entities. Small value objects such as component rules and grade bands live in validated RuleVersion JSON; they do not need independent editable tables. SQL migrations add constraints and RLS that the ORM schema alone cannot express.

# 6 Transactions and API contracts

## API conventions

Use /api/v1, JSON, opaque UUIDs and cursor pagination capped at 100. Response envelopes carry data and requestId; errors carry code, message and fieldErrors without SQL details. Use 401 for unauthenticated, 403 for forbidden actions, 404 for inaccessible IDs, 409 for stale/concurrent state and 422 for invalid business input.

PATCH commands require expectedVersion. Side-effect POST commands require Idempotency-Key scoped to tenant, actor and operation; store request hash and result for 24 hours. Reusing a key with a different body returns 409. Commands store audit in their business transaction.

| **Command**                       | **Essential input**                  | **Required gate**                                            |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| POST /exams                       | termId, mode, subjects, rule         | Controller; valid configuration and enrolled subjects.       |
| POST /exams/{id}/registrations    | selectedSubjectIds                   | Own student; window open and eligible enrolment.             |
| POST /registrations/{id}/approve  | expectedVersion                      | Controller; recomputed eligibility and no duplicate.         |
| PUT /papers/{id}/allocation       | hallIds, studentIds, expectedVersion | Controller; capacity, approved roster and no time conflicts. |
| POST /exams/{id}/publish-schedule | expectedVersion                      | All papers, seats and accepted duty coverage ready.          |
| PUT /sittings/{id}/attendance     | entries, expectedVersion             | Assigned accepted invigilator in conduct window.             |
| POST /marks-batches/{id}/submit   | expectedVersion                      | Assigned examiner; complete permitted marks.                 |
| POST /marks-batches/{id}/approve  | expectedVersion, reason              | Reviewer scope; not submitter; submitted state.              |
| POST /exams/{id}/result-runs      | expectedVersion                      | Controller; approved batches and closed conduct.             |
| POST /exams/{id}/publications     | runId, expectedVersion               | Current revision, approved gates and no active publication.  |
| GET /me/results/{examId}          | Session identity                     | Own active published StudentResult only.                     |

## Concurrency controls

Allocation and timetable changes use a tenant/campus transaction advisory lock, recheck half-open time overlaps \[start,end), and write seats atomically. Every scheduling and assignment path must take the same lock. Unique constraints backstop duplicate seats. Marks updates use conditional version changes; stale saves cannot silently replace another editor. Result-affecting commands lock the exam before subordinate records in a consistent order.

# 7 Files jobs and operations

## File lifecycle

Restrict question papers to PDF, proposed maximum 20 MB. Imports accept CSV/XLSX up to 5 MB and 500 students or 5,000 component-mark rows per job. Reject macro-enabled workbooks, encrypted files, invalid signatures and unsupported formats. Bound decompression, sheet counts and parser memory.

A requested upload receives a tenant-specific private quarantine key. After upload, validate content and scan it in a worker. Only CLEAN documents may be bound to a paper or downloaded. A scan outage leaves PENDING; staff cannot bypass it. Downloads require permission, assignment and availability-window checks on every request; issue short-lived private links, proposed 60 seconds. Link expiry limits exposure but cannot revoke a copy already downloaded. \[T3\]

Admit and grade-card PDFs use institution branding, an issue/version identifier and an input checksum. Grades render from immutable StudentResult snapshots. Reissuing a schedule revokes the current admit-card reference and queues a new version; old generated files remain auditable and are not returned as current.

## Operational design

Keep API and worker health endpoints separate. Readiness checks database access and required configuration. Monitor request latency/error rate, database saturation, old job leases, dead jobs, rejected authorization, missing marks and stale result runs. Logs contain tenant ID, actor ID and request ID but no tokens, question content or complete marks payloads.

Automated database backups and point-in-time recovery are a pilot prerequisite. Proposed recovery targets are RPO 24 hours and RTO 4 hours; verify by restoring a representative backup before real data use. Enable object versioning and define matching retention. Do not label these targets as achieved until the drill succeeds.

Retention is a tenant contract decision before pilot. Proposed pilot defaults are 30 days for quarantined failed uploads and temporary imports, and 90 days for operational logs; do not automatically delete academic history, grades or audit records in the MVP. Access to student information follows least privilege. This design makes no regulatory certification claim.

## Failure recovery

Workers can resume after crashes using leases and unique keys. Failed imports commit no domain rows. Failed PDF generation leaves a visible retryable status. A stale result run is recomputed. Database migration failure stops rollout; deploy a compatible prior application image or restore only with an explicit data-loss assessment.

# 9 Engineering decisions and references

| **Decision**               | **Reason**                                                     | **Consequence**                                                          |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Modular monolith           | Shared transactions and a small sprint team                    | Enforce module ownership in code review; avoid internal HTTP services.   |
| PostgreSQL plus RLS        | Relational workflows and defence against missed tenant filters | Requires SQL migrations, scoped transaction clients and isolation tests. |
| Fixed workflow commands    | Clear acceptance in three days                                 | No general workflow designer or arbitrary status PATCH endpoint.         |
| Immutable result snapshots | Reproducible published grades                                  | Corrections require withdrawal, new approval/run and new publication.    |
| Database jobs              | Fewer operational components for pilot                         | Monitor queue growth; isolate worker load from API traffic.              |
| One regular attempt        | Keeps enrolment, attendance and result keys clear              | Reattempts and historic CGPA require a future schema/rules extension.    |
| Private file storage       | Papers and student PDFs require explicit access                | No public bucket or anonymous document routes.                           |

## Deployment and repository shape

Use apps/web, apps/api and apps/worker with packages/contracts and packages/domain for shared types and pure result functions. Keep Prisma schema and SQL migrations under packages/db. Do not share server credentials or server-only modules with the web bundle. Lock dependency versions and container digests in the implementation repository after a clean compatibility build.

The pilot uses one isolated environment with fictional demo tenants. Production and staging must have separate credentials, database and storage prefixes/buckets. CI runs required tests, builds images, scans dependencies and applies reviewed forward-compatible migrations once. Schema rollback is not automatic.

## Architecture acceptance

No source implementation is represented as complete by this document. Engineering must demonstrate tenant-safe queries, transaction rollback, concurrent command handling, file authorization, result determinism and backup recovery using the Implementation Document's release gates.
